research_question: Calculate the distance of a new Paint-billed Crake observation in Leticia, Colombia to the nearest historical occurrence record to determine its range extension.

phase_1.user_prompt: I recently observed a Paint-billed Crake (Mustelirallus erythrops) at the airport in Leticia, Amazonas, Colombia. I want to check how far this observation is from known populations to document a potential range extension. Could you search for all historical occurrence data for this species in Colombia, up to March 3, 2020 (when I started my analysis), to use as a baseline?

phase_2.user_prompt: Please download the historical occurrence dataset for the Paint-billed Crake in Colombia that you just identified.

phase_3.user_prompt: Now, I need to calculate the distance from my new sighting to all the historical records. My observation was at coordinates 04°11′44″S, 069°56′34″W. Please compute the distance in kilometers from this location to every historical point you downloaded.

phase_4.user_prompt: What is the minimum distance to a historical record, and what does this indicate about the species' known range? Additionally, please generate a map showing the historical records and my new observation point (marked clearly in red) to visualize the range extension. Save the map as `crake_range_extension_map.png`.

checkpoint.reference_conclusion: The new record represents a significant distribution extension of over 800 km into the Colombian Amazon, far southeast of previously known and patchy records in the Andes and foothills.
checkpoint.visual_description: A map of Colombia (and surrounding regions) showing historical occurrence points mostly clustered in the western/central regions (Andes/foothills) and a single, distinctively marked (e.g., red) new observation point in the extreme southeast corner of Colombia near Leticia.
